item.title: U-17 Women’s World ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌​⁠​‍‌​​‌​Cup: Flamingos face North Korea in crucial clash
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos face a stern test against defending champions Korea DPR on Friday as they seek to secure a place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Korea DPR, two-time champions since the competition began in New Zealand in 2008, have been impressive, winning their opening two matches to top Group B. The North Koreans have scored 12 goals and conceded only one, underlining their attacking strength as they pursue another title. Nigeria, bronze medallists in 2022, are seeking to keep their campaign alive after losing 2-1 to Poland before recovering with a 2-0 victory over tournament debutants Puerto Rico. The Flamingos will need a disciplined performance against the defending champions, with qualification for the knockout stage still within reach. A win or draw would guarantee Nigeria’s progress, while a defeat would leave their chances dependent on the outcome of the Poland-Puerto Rico match and the applicable tiebreakers. The two teams have met twice at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, with Nigeria winning 3-2 in 2010 before Korea DPR recorded a 3-0 victory in 2016. Coach Akeem Busari and his players will need to remain defensively organised and take their chances against a North Korean side that has dominated its group matches. item.title: 2027: Atiku suffering from ‘Emir complex’ — Segun Sowunmi
item.description: Segun Sowunmi, a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of being disconnected from the struggles of ordinary Nigerians, saying he suffers from what he described as an “Emir complex”. Sowunmi made the remarks during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub , while assessing President Bola Tinubu’s chances of re-election in 2027 and responding to opposition leaders who argue that the contest will be between the ruling APC and Nigerians, regardless of the number of governors backing the president. The APC chieftain questioned the credibility of opposition figures, including Atiku and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, to speak for Nigerians grappling with poverty, given their long years in public office. He said Amaechi had spent much of his political career in government before recently positioning himself as a voice against poverty in the country. “The opposition that all of their lives, they have just been eating from both sides of their mouths like Rotimi Amaechi, who spent the last 24 years, minus the time that they asked him to go and sit down somewhere; he has been in government, and suddenly Rotimi is the epitome that’s going to tell you that there’s poverty in Nigeria?” he asked. Sowunmi also questioned Atiku’s ability to understand the experiences of poor Nigerians, pointing to his time as vice president under former President Olusegun Obasanjo from 1999 to 2007 and his public profile. “Up till today, Atiku was vice president 1999 to 2007, that’s when he stopped his vice presidency,” he said. Describing what he called an “Emir complex”, Sowunmi argued that Atiku’s lifestyle and public demeanour made it difficult for him to empathise with people struggling to make ends meet. “Up till today, have you seen vice president that goes around the way Atiku is going around with convoy, in terms of his panache, Atiku is suffering from what you call an Emir complex,” he said. Explaining the phrase, Sowunmi said it referred to a powerful figure accustomed to being treated with deference by people around him. “You know what an Emir complex is? That big man that everybody will just come and say, ‘Dan labayi; ranka dede;’ or an oba complex,” he said. He added that Atiku was not qualified to present himself as a champion of the poor. “So he has no capacity to know or empathise with the poor. He is not a patron deity of the poor,” Sowunmi said. The APC campaign council member maintained that the opposition’s criticism of Tinubu and his administration should be assessed against the records of those making the claims. Tinubu is seeking another term in 2027, with APC governors and some governors elected on other party platforms among those who have declared support for his re-election bid. item.title: One dead, three rescued in Lagos building collapse
item.description: The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) has confirmed one death and the rescue of three adult males following the collapse of a two-storey building under construction in Fadeyi, Lagos. The Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday in Lagos. Oke-Osanyintolu ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌​⁠​‍‍‍‌‌​said the incident occurred in the early hours of Friday at Akinola Street, by Fadeyi Bus Stop, off Ikorodu Road. He said search and rescue operations were ongoing to determine whether more persons were trapped beneath the rubble. He said the agency received a distress call at 12:10 a.m., prompting the immediate activation of its Cobra Response Team from Onipanu Base. According to him, the team arrived at the scene at 12:12 a.m. and discovered that the building under construction had collapsed, with construction workers suspected to be trapped beneath the debris. Oke-Osanyintolu said search and rescue operations commenced immediately, with safety measures put in place to protect victims and emergency responders. He added that groaning sounds were heard beneath the rubble during the operation, indicating possible survivors. He said the agency deployed an excavator to facilitate the search and rescue operation. Oke-Osanyintolu said the rescued victims received immediate pre-hospital care from LASEMA paramedics and the Lagos State Ambulance Service (LASAMBUS) before being transferred to hospital. He listed the responders at the scene as the LASEMA Response Team, Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, LASAMBUS and officers of the Nigeria Police Force from Alagbon Division. He said the cause of the collapse had yet to be determined and would be investigated by relevant regulatory agencies. He commiserated with the family of the deceased and wished the rescued victims a speedy recovery. He also reiterated the government’s commitment to tackling substandard construction and strengthening monitoring and enforcement in collaboration with the Lagos State Building Control Agency to prevent similar incidents. item.description: By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor RECENTLY, an unprecedented interview session with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo broke the Internet. Obasanjo is one of the most interviewed Nigerians ever, yet this interview was different, specifically because it was conducted by Adebayo Ridwan Abidemi, more popularly known as Isbae U. The interview, which succeeded in revealing a side of the statesman that had never been obvious to the public, garnered millions of views within the first 24 hours and continues to fascinate viewers because of its sheer creativity, audacity and innovation. The YouTube chat, during which Abidemi referred to the former president as his “tenant” and “employee” for eight years, is a classic illustration of the contrast between the old and new generations, highlighting the conservatism of the older generation and the audacity of the younger one. item.content:encoded: By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor RECENTLY, an unprecedented interview session with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo broke the Internet. Obasanjo is one of the most interviewed Nigerians ever, yet this interview was different, specifically because it was conducted by Adebayo Ridwan Abidemi, more popularly known as Isbae U. The interview, which succeeded in revealing a side of the statesman that had never been obvious to the public, garnered millions of views within the first 24 hours and continues to fascinate viewers because of its sheer creativity, audacity and innovation. The YouTube chat, during which Abidemi referred to the former president as his “tenant” and “employee” for eight years, is a classic illustration of the contrast between the old and new generations, highlighting the conservatism of the older generation and the audacity of the younger one. On the other hand, 15 former nursing students who were recently suspended or expelled following the publication of a video in August were not so lucky. The young women, who participated in a viral video captioned “No sick oo, na Gen Z full hospital”, were apparently taking part in a “challenge”—a term used to describe the replication of particular digital content for the purpose of trending online. Generational ‘Wars’ Are Normal, But… Abidemi and the 15 nursing students were displaying behaviours characteristic of a generation known as Gen Z. Some love them, some hate them, some vilify them; while others admire them. Generations are groups of people born within roughly the same period who may share similar historical experiences, cultural influences, technologies and social values. These labels are commonly used in sociology, marketing, media and workplace research. Every generation has regarded the ones that follow as somewhat morally inferior. However, criticism of Gen Z does not seem to fall within the typical complaints about youthful exuberance that have persisted across generations. The major concern is that Gen Z appears to have a disdain for, and disregard for, well-established societal, social and professional norms. “What sets Gen Z apart,” says Olatoun Lufadeju, a Lagos-based sociologist, “is that they seem to be the only living generation that does not defer to age. They don’t associate wisdom with age or even experience. “For them, the generations before them have failed them and have been unable to give them a better life. They think, if you are so smart, why is the country like this? Why is the world like this? We should actually listen to them.” As far as Lufadeju is concerned, the upsides of the generation’s characteristics far outweigh the downsides. Asked to comment on the expulsion and suspension of the Madonna University students, she told Vanguard, “Is there an actual law against dancing? Seriously, I am asking not rhetorically. I might be wrong.” Your Negativity, Their Creativity Despite the admiration for their resilience, most members of older generations regard Gen Z with wariness, at best. The 15 Madonna University students, despite the initial public outrage, have nevertheless garnered considerable sympathy over the disciplinary actions taken against them, particularly given that they were all in their fifth and final year at the School of Nursing. Amnesty International has weighed in on the expulsion and suspension of the TikTok dancers, describing the actions as “disproportionate”. The organisation’s published statement reads: “Imposing heavy-handed academic or disciplinary sanctions would terminate the academic progress of the affected students. The students have the rights to freedom of expression, academic freedom and education. The expulsion and suspension are harsh and would create a chilling effect on the enjoyment of these rights.” The organization called on the university to ensure that its disciplinary policies and procedures comply with international human rights standards. A Social Contagion? While Gen Z is widely perceived as using negativity to make a point, its members do not necessarily have anything to prove. Nonconformity, by its very nature, does not always require justification. A quick online poll conducted by Vanguard on the subject asked: “Gen Z is completely rewriting the rules for school, work, and life. If you had to define their ultimate mindset, which trait takes the crown?” Some 33.3 per cent of respondents described them as “unbound or free”, while 28.6 per cent described them as “nonconformist”; another 14.3 per cent said they were “fluid” or “always varying”, while 23.8 per cent described them as “pragmatic” and “system hacks”. A UNICEF-led private-sector partnership study, however, found that despite their resilience, creativity and determination, a worrying combination of geopolitical conflicts, climate and ecological crisis, economic slowdowns and mental health challenges is leaving young people feeling overwhelmed, disconnected and adrift, without adequate mental health support or services. The study, based on a survey of more than 1,000 Gen Z respondents aged 14-25 worldwide, found that, contrary to the beliefs of other generations, Gen Z is deeply engaged with global issues and consumes more news than any other form of content. Its members are also eager to help shape the future. New Life Realitie Born during the dot-com era, Gen Z did not have to acclimatize to a digital world. Rather, its members grew up helping to define it. As the generation prepared to enter the job market, the world was hit by the COVID-19 pandemic and the ensuing global shutdowns, accelerating the adoption of remote work—a development that has helped shape Gen Z’s attitude towards employment. Iyin Aboyeji, a millennial and founder of two billion-dollar companies, found himself in the bad books of Gen Z after publishing a highly controversial LinkedIn article suggesting that young people should work in person during the early stages of their careers. He stated, “What AI cannot automate is proximity, the senior colleague who corrects your first draft, the room where decisions are made and the peer mentorship and networking that build the skills for us which tomorrow’s business deals are built.” While members of older generations largely agreed with him, the backlash from Gen Z was phenomenal, targeted a usually beloved tech guru whom many young people look up to. For them, even workplace networking can be disrupted. One response read, “Working on-site for me isn’t a problem, but for a young person in Nigeria in 2026, what does that cost me in terms of finances, physically, and mentally? There are infrastructural problems that make it harder for a young person such as myself.” Is the Rash of Information Shaping Gen Z’s Attitudes? item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 23, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira exchanged at around N1,330.95 to the US Dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). The official window opened with early spot transactions hovering around N1,330.95 to N1,332.00 per dollar, maintaining relative stability following recent daily fluctuations. In the unofficial parallel market, street traders and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across major commercial hubs, including Lagos and Abuja, quoted buying rates around N1,360 to N1,365 per dollar, while selling rates traded between N1,375 and N1,380 per dollar. The gap between the official NFEM rate and the parallel market continues to reflect ongoing demand from retail buyers, small business importers, and individuals seeking foreign currency for international travel and tuition payments. At current trading levels, exchanging $100 yields approximately N133,095 through official banking and NFEM channels, compared to up to N138,000 when purchased through parallel market operators. Market participants attribute current rate stability to sustained diaspora remittance inflows alongside foreign portfolio interest in domestic yield instruments. item.title: NYSC kidnap: DSS witness exposes how suspects were identified
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — A Department of State Services, DSS, operative yesterday told an Imo State High Court how 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members were abducted at gunpoint while travelling to orientation camps, as hearing began in the case against three alleged kidnappers. The witness, Ikechukwu Emmanuel, who investigated the incident, said the victims and one of the bus drivers identified the three defendants during an identification parade. The defendants, Usman Aliyu, alias Chonge; Babangida Aliyu; and Mohamed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper, are standing trial on a three-count charge of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms in suit number HOU/22C/2026. Testifying before Justice Emeka Orafu, the DSS operative said the incident occurred at about 6.30am on October 1, 2026, when the 20 prospective corps members were travelling in two buses from Ibadan to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. He told the court that armed men wielding AK-47 rifles attacked the buses and took all 20 passengers hostage, moving them into the bush. According to the witness, security agencies in Imo State, including the DSS, launched operations using human and technical intelligence to track the kidnappers and secure the victims’ release. He said the hostages were eventually released after the payment of ransom demanded by the kidnappers, while investigations continued. Emmanuel further told the court that intelligence reports indicated that the suspects had moved to Rivers and Abia states, leading to their arrest between October 10 and 14, 2026. Explaining the identification process, the witness said the three defendants were placed among 10 other persons during an identification parade. He said the abducted prospective corps members and one of the bus drivers identified them. The witness also told the court that Usman Aliyu, in his confessional statement, said 11 persons participated in the kidnap operation. The Imo State Director of Public Prosecutions, Mr Martins Udolwu, led the prosecution team, while Mr Nnaemeka S.C. Adipo and Mr Paschal Ofoma represented the defendants. After the witness’s evidence-in-chief, Justice Orafu adjourned the case to October 27, 28 and 29, 2026, for continuation of hearing. The judge urged the defence to be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately after the conclusion of his evidence-in-chief, stressing that he did not want the trial to extend into the new year. “The Defence must be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately he is done with his evidence in chief,” the judge said. item.title: Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has died at the age of 57 following a brief illness, his family has announced. The family announced his death in a statement posted on the actor’s official Instagram page in the early hours of Friday, expressing appreciation to fans and well-wishers for their prayers and support. “We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. “We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen,” the statement read. Duru is survived by his wife, Adokiye, and children Duru, who began his acting career in 1989, became widely known for his role as Ahanna in Rattlesnake , the 1995 film produced by the late filmmaker Amaka Igwe. His death comes months after he dismissed reports that he was battling a life-threatening illness, describing footage circulating online in June as false. In a video posted on Instagram in response to the reports, the actor rejected claims about his health and criticised those circulating the footage. Born on July 27, 1969, in Cameroon to Nigerian parents from Imo State, Duru completed his primary and secondary education in Cameroon before moving to Nigeria for university studies. He studied Theatre Arts at the University of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1996. Duru made his film debut in Missing Mark in 1989, in a production directed by the late Ndubuisi Oko. His performance in Rattlesnake later established him as a recognised face in Nollywood. Over his decades-long career, he featured in several Nigerian films, including Blood Money (1997), Stigma (2013) and Mboputa (2020). In 2020, he won the Best Actor in a Leading Role (Igbo) award at the Best of Nollywood Awards for his performance in Mboputa . He also received the United Nations Ambassador of Peace award in 2007 in recognition of his influence on young people. Duru served as interim president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria in 2010 and was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role at the Africa Movie Academy Awards that year. Atiku said Nigerians could not verify the commission’s claim that more than 103 million voters had been registered when the register was reportedly unavailable on its online portal during the October 9 to 15 inspection period. In a statement on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded the immediate publication of the register, questioning conflicting accounts of when it was displayed and raising concerns about safeguards against electoral fraud. “INEC has announced more than 103 million registered voters. item.title: FIFA okays Normalisation Committee to run Nigerian football
item.description: The Bureau of the FIFA Council on Thursday approved the appointment of a Normalisation Committee to manage the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation, pending fresh elections into the NFF Executive Committee. According to a letter signed by FIFA Secretary General, Mattias Grafström and addressed to Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme MON, “the normalisation committee shall consist of a suitable number of members, who will be appointed jointly by FIFA and CAF as soon as possible.” The letter also informed that “the period during which the normalisation committee shall perform its functions shall expire as soon as it has fulfilled all of its tasks, but by no later than 31 May 2027.” None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances. In the meantime, the Secretariat of the NFF will continue with the day-to-day running of the organisation and administration of the country’s football pending the appointment of the Normalisation Committee. item.title: IPOB member pleads guilty, jailed 20 years for belonging to proscribed group
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja, on Thursday, convicted and sentenced a self-confessed member of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Mr. Paul Okechukwu, 48, to 20 years in prison for belonging to a proscribed organisation. The defendant pleaded guilty to one count of a two-count charge the Federal Government preferred against him. The Federal Government alleged in the first count that the defendant, who is from Nnewi South in Anambra State, had in 2021, while in Imo State, committed an offence by belonging to IPOB, a proscribed organisation, contrary to and punishable under Section 16 of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. In the second count, the Federal Government alleged that the defendant participated in an attack in which two security operatives were killed, and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 2(1) of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. After the charge was read to him, the defendant pleaded not guilty to the second count. In view of this development, and following an application by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who was in court to lead the prosecution, the court struck out the second count after it was withdrawn. Relying on Section 72 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022, the Attorney-General applied for the court to allow a witness from the Department of State Services (DSS) to review some facts of the case. The witness, whose name was given as “ABC” for the purpose of the trial, identified the defendant as a member of IPOB, which he said had since been outlawed. He told the court that the defendant was involved in acts of terrorism, which he said included attacks on security agents. The witness, who said he was part of a team that investigated the defendant, tendered a copy of the report, which was admitted as Exhibit A. While applying for the defendant to be convicted, the AGF argued that the law prescribed a minimum sentence of 20 years for the offence. “We therefore urge my lord to impose the maximum sentence, at least to serve as a deterrent to others and to also show that the nation cannot condone any act of terrorism,” the AGF added. Meanwhile, immediately after the AGF made the application, the defendant broke down in tears in the dock, begging the court to temper justice with mercy. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Hawa Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 20 years. The court said it took note of the charge against the defendant and “the ripple effect it has on the nation.” It held that the defendant should be remanded in any correctional facility chosen by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service to serve his sentence, which should count from the day he was arrested. item.title: N10bn untouched – APC accuses Atiku of politicising Ebola response
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President, Atiku Abubakar, of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, insisting that approved emergency funds remain untouched. The council’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. Alake said President Bola Tinubu approved N10 billion for the Ebola emergency in June, but relevant agencies deployed other available resources. “On accountability, the Atiku camp should note that the N10 billion the President approved for the Ebola emergency in June remains untouched,” he said. He said the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and other agencies strengthened surveillance at entry points. According to him, the surveillance network alerted the government to the index case and facilitated contact tracing for 44 contacts. The council commended the agencies for their contributions to monitoring the Ebola threat and supporting the public health response. It also criticised Atiku’s reference linking President Tinubu’s name to Ebola, saying it risked turning a serious health concern into political ridicule. “We believe linking and rhyming President Bola Tinubu’s name to Ebola only risks turning a serious health concern into a vehicle to ridicule the President,” Alake said. The council also defended the handling of the infected Nigerian’s detection, citing the virus’s incubation period and the timing of symptoms. “For anyone infected with the virus, the incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, with symptoms typically appearing eight to 10 days after exposure. “An infected person cannot spread or transmit Ebola to others until they actively develop symptoms,” he said. Alake urged opposition politicians to support health authorities rather than criticise the government’s response to the public health threat. “A responsible opposition will applaud the Task Force for being responsive. But the Atiku camp always goes for cheap shots at the government,” he said. The council also rejected Atiku’s allegation that a ministerial briefing was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies or voting. Alake described the allegation as speculative, adding that the briefing instead urged Nigerians to comply with protocols announced by the task force. He called on Atiku and his supporters to avoid politicising public health concerns, urging Nigerians to shun rumours and follow health authorities’ guidance. “We advise Atiku Abubakar and his hirelings to avoid politicising public health issues,” he said. The council said protecting Nigerians from the deadly disease should remain the priority. item.title: Saving Nigeria from the increasingly absurd theatrics of Jimoh Ibrahim, by Owei Lakemfa
item.description: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu this week featured prominently in the newest theatre of the absurd staged by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Folorunsho Ibrahim. The stage was the Aso Rock Presidential Villa, Abuja, where, on October 19, 2026, Ibrahim presented the seven-volume UN 2027 draft budget to President Tinubu. Ibrahim began the comedy with a big, fat lie. He claimed: “This is the first time in 66 years that Nigeria will chair the Budget and Administration Committee. It is the first time, and we do not know when it will happen again in history.” Contrary to this wild claim, the first time Nigeria chaired the UN Budget and Administration Committee was on September 22, 1971. item.content:encoded: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu this week featured prominently in the newest theatre of the absurd staged by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Folorunsho Ibrahim. The stage was the Aso Rock Presidential Villa, Abuja, where, on October 19, 2026, Ibrahim presented the seven-volume UN 2027 draft budget to President Tinubu. Ibrahim began the comedy with a big, fat lie. He claimed: “This is the first time in 66 years that Nigeria will chair the Budget and Administration Committee. It is the first time, and we do not know when it will happen again in history.” Contrary to this wild claim, the first time Nigeria chaired the UN Budget and Administration Committee was on September 22, 1971. This is verifiable in UN records, including its digitallibrary.un.org. That 1971 date was when Ambassador Edward Olu Sanu was elected the UN Budget Committee Chair. At that time, Ibrahim was a four-year-old boy. So, contrary to Ibrahim’s claim that it took Nigeria 66 years after independence to be elected chair of the UN Budget Committee, the country was actually chair within eleven years of its independence. Ibrahim followed this falsehood with the announcement that: “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is making history by being able to receive this budget. He is the first Nigerian president in 66 years to receive the UN budget from the United Nations.” May Tinubu be the first and last Nigerian President to be subjected to this absurdity. The UN draft budget is not Nigeria’s budget. It is that of the 193 Member countries of the UN and is slated for deliberations at the UN Headquarters in New York, not in the Nigerian Presidency. So, what does Ibrahim want President Tinubu to do with the seven volumes? Sit down and read them? For what purpose? Can Tinubu amend, audit, veto or pass the UN budget? Why would Ibrahim’s publicity stunt be allowed to subject Nigeria to international ridicule? All ambassadors report to the Foreign Affairs Minister. Did Ibrahim pass through Minister Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu before presenting the unofficial UN budget to President Tinubu? Did she, as procedures dictate, even approve his journey to Abuja? If she did, was the Foreign Ministry part of this charade? This is the second time within three months that Ibrahim would be disgracing Nigeria. In July 2026, he held a press conference and announced that: “President Tinubu will be sitting very close to Donald Trump in the front row of the United Nations General Assembly. Don’t ask me how that was arranged, but he will be sitting.” He gave the impression that the UN is a corrupt organisation where sitting positions can be purchased. Secondly, he presents the slavish mentality that it will be a rare privilege for Tinubu to sit close to Trump. Ibrahim’s claims about the sitting arrangement in the UN are false. For the UNGA meetings, the arrangement is determined alphabetically by the English name of each country. The starting position is based on a random annual lottery in which the UN Secretary-General picks the name of a Member State from a box. The country so picked is assigned the first seat in the hall, which is the far right of the front row from the podium. After this, the remaining 192 countries are seated round the hall, with each entitled to six seats: three for delegates and three for alternates. This arrangement is valid for one year and affects the sitting arrangements for all formal meetings of the UN Committees. This month, when I was in the UN to make a case for the complete decolonisation of Western Sahara, I had the privilege of visiting the UNGA Hall. So, Nigeria already had its allocated sixth position, sitting in the front row of the General Assembly chamber for the 2026 UNGA, before Ibrahim appeared at the Presidential Villa to claim that he had a special seat for Tinubu close to where Trump is to sit. Therefore, when Vice President Kashim Shettima, who represented Tinubu at UNGA 2026, sat in the sixth position and Ibrahim proclaimed that it was a significant diplomatic achievement, it was a lie. The UN sitting arrangement is in line with UN principles of the sovereign equality of states. So, no country has a permanent front-row seat. Nigeria has a long, glorious history of diplomacy. As far back as 1486, that is, 540 years ago, the Benin Kingdom, under Oba Ozolua in present-day Edo State, had an ambassador in the Court of King John II of Portugal. In 1526, Benin, under Oba Esigie, had an ambassador to Europe as well as an embassy building in Lisbon. In return, Portugal sent ambassadors to the Benin Oba’s Court. The Itsekiri Kingdom in present-day Delta State had accredited ambassadors to the Vatican and European Courts. So, if territories that are now part of Nigeria had accredited ambassadors to Europe over five centuries ago, it is tragic that we would be presenting Nigeria today as a country that lacks diplomatic knowledge or experience. It is indeed quite disgraceful that a country that had outstanding Permanent Representatives to the UN, such as Chief Simeon Adebo, Emeka Anyaoku, Ibrahim Gambari, who became one of the most outstanding UN envoys, and Joseph Garba, who was the face of the Anti-Apartheid Movement in the UN, would appoint a Jimoh Ibrahim to such a prominent position as Nigeria’s face in the world assembly. Ibrahim is a disaster waiting to happen. In my July 2026 column titled ‘Jimoh Ibrahim is uninformed: UN intervenes in nation’s internal affairs’, I had observed that his knowledge of diplomacy is weak and advised him “to read the UN Charter, its main resolutions and practices”. I had also observed that he does not appear to listen to good advice. So, I suggested that he listen to our career ambassadors in the UN. Perhaps, if he had done so, he would not continue scripting absurd pieces of drama in the world body. However, this is not about Jimoh Ibrahim, who, sooner or later, will leave. This is about our country. I think the Foreign Ministry and our Foreign Ministers should exercise proper supervision of our ambassadors, especially the non-career ones like Jimoh Ibrahim, who may not be experienced in diplomacy. We should also ensure that people so appointed or sent to foreign missions are knowledgeable, teachable and respectable. I have had it said a few times that President Tinubu is his own Foreign Minister. No! This was what was touted about President Muhammadu Buhari, and it ended up disastrous. President Tinubu should concentrate on his job of ensuring the welfare and security of Nigerians and give the Foreign Ministry and the Foreign Ministers he has willingly chosen a free hand to run our international affairs. item.title: 2027 Election: Even Tinubu Knows Atiku Is The Best Candidate – Momodu
item.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communications of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign, Dele Momodu, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as the best candidate for the 2027 election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Momodu said Atiku had been the most deliberate and focused candidate since he first sought the presidency in 1993. The ADC chieftain claimed that President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), also knows that the former vice president is better suited for the job. “When I say he (Atiku) is the best, it is a statement of fact and even President Bola Tinubu himself knows that,” Momodu said. “That is why at a time, he invited him and they joined hands for Atiku to run in the past.” ﻿ Comparing the credentials of the three major presidential candidates, Momodu said Tinubu’s strongest credential was his tenure as governor of Lagos State, while Atiku’s was his experience as vice president and Peter Obi’s as governor of Anambra State. He argued that Tinubu had underestimated the differences between governing Lagos and leading Nigeria. “So, if you look at the three mainstream candidates today, the APC candidate Bola Tinubu, the ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar and the NDC candidate Peter Obi, you can judge for yourself. Bola Tinubu came, his best credential was being the former governor of Lagos State; Atiku came, his best credential was being the former vice president of Nigeria; Peter Obi came, his best credential was being the governor of Anambra State. “So, if you judge for yourself, you will know that perhaps what has happened to President Tinubu is the fact that when he got to the Presidency, he assumed that Nigeria was Lagos and he soon discovered that Nigeria is different from Lagos and that is why he’s had total commotional confusion and his guys are running all over the places throwing money around.” Momodu also accused the Tinubu administration of failing to be sincere with Nigerians, alleging that officials around the President were more concerned with telling him what he wanted to hear than confronting him with the realities facing the country. “What is lacking in this government is that sincerity. Everything is about one man. The people who are running our economy today have to tell Nigerians only what they think the president wants to hear. They are not telling him the truth, and when tomorrow comes, he will realise it,” he added. item.title: Tinubu Tasks Medical Experts On Brain Drain Solutions In West Africa
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged the West African College of Physicians (WACP) to develop practical and sustainable solutions to medical brain drain across the sub-region, warning that the migration of skilled professionals continues to put pressure on healthcare systems. He said the trend limits access to essential medical services and increases the workload on available health personnel. According to a statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu spoke on Thursday after being conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja. He urged the College’s leadership to use its forthcoming conference to develop lasting solutions to the challenge. “We are more challenged in Africa than anywhere else; you know, and with the outbreak of Ebola now we’re looking for a preventive action that will eliminate all these problems and infections. So, I wish you the best. As I pledge to behave myself, I will continue to do whatever I can do for this honourable profession,” the President said. Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to comprehensive health sector reforms aimed at making healthcare delivery more accessible, affordable and efficient for Nigerians. He also commended the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, for driving the reforms. “We as a government are doing everything possible. Please help me congratulate the reform-oriented physician, Ali Pate, who has been doing a very good job,” he said. President Tinubu was conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency The President acknowledged medical professionals’ contributions to medical research, disease prevention, life-saving interventions and the development of resilient healthcare systems capable of responding to existing and emerging health challenges.
